Actually I'm not entirely sure if we should keep it, it's a _very_ specific debugging tool. IIRC the idea is to keep only the proxy running (skipping the rest of the engine) so that you can throw specific third-party clients at it (e.g. `wayland-info`) and see how it reacts to them.

body:
I missed that we were adding a `thirdparty/mesa` folder. Likewise, the goal of thirdparty folders isn't to follow the upstream structure as is, but we trim it down to only what we need, so all these intermediary folders are unnecessary.

I think it's a bit overkill to add a top-level folder just for one XML file, and it's also confusing as we do use bits of Mesa for D3D12 via https://github.com/godotengine/godot-nir-static.

I'd prefer to just put it under `thirdparty/wayland-protocols/mesa/wayland-drm.xml`.

And yeah the license in `wayland-drm.xml` is the `X11` license: https://spdx.org/licenses/X11.html
(older MIT derivative)
